subject: Networking & air-gap viability — next tests and competitive fit
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Gates <alan.gates@greenfieldfin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Jun 2028 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Networking & air-gap viability — recap and immediate asks

Alan — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned as you evaluate Redwood vs hyperscaler alternatives: 

- Primary constraints you reiterated: full air-gap option for inference (no outbound control plane), on-prem GPU pool integration, and audit logs for every inference request.
- Competitive lens: you mentioned HypCloud is offering a managed private endpoint but still requires periodic outbound control-plane heartbeats; you want to validate whether that breaks your compliance posture.

Attached are three items we promised on the call: a short feasibility matrix (controlplane-feasibility-matrix.xlsx), a network test plan (network-test-plan.md), and a concise feature-differentiator brief (redwood-vs-hypcloud-comparison.pdf).

Immediate asks for your team: 
1) Can you confirm whether your security team can provision a jump host / bastion IP we can use for an inbound-only verification test? If yes, please provide IP(s) and an allowed port window for 48 hours.
2) Share the vendor questionnaire excerpt you mentioned (SOC2 section + network diagrams) — we can pre-fill items related to our private deployment.

Planned next steps from our side: 
- Ben will draft a technical test that demonstrates a truly air-gapped Redwood Private setup (control plane running fully on customer network / HSM-integrated).
- Marissa will align contract language options for an isolated control plane clause and a short-term SLA for the POC.

Can you please confirm availability for a 45-minute technical session with your infra and security leads on Monday (Jun 22) or Tuesday (Jun 23)?

Thanks — want to make sure we give you the clearest evidence differentiating us from the managed-hyperscaler approach.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Alan Gates <alan.gates@greenfieldfin.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@greenfieldfin.com, infra@greenfieldfin.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:18:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Networking & air-gap viability — recap and immediate asks

Thanks, Soojin — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide a bastion IP for a 48-hour window next week. Security would prefer inbound TLS to terminate on our side; we cannot accept outbound persistent control-plane connections to third-party hosts without an approved exception.
- I attached the vendor questionnaire PDF you asked for (redacted). The key sections are network topology and key management.

Two quick technical clarifications: 
1) When you say "control plane on customer network", do you mean a private controller that polls the Redwood orchestrator (pull) or a local controller that accepts inbound API calls from your control plane (push)? We need explicit data flow diagrams.
2) For KV caching and checkpointing of model state, where would logs and audit trails be written? We need an architecture that keeps PII off any external telemetry.

We are available for the technical session on Tue Jun 23 10:00–11:00 EDT.

Alan Gates
CTO, Greenfield Financial
[attachment: vendor-questionnaire-sample.pdf (pdf)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Gates <alan.gates@greenfieldfin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 11:01:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Networking & air-gap viability — recap and immediate asks

Alan — great, thanks for the notes and the questionnaire. High-level answers below to help you prep the security review; Ben will take the deep-dive in the tech session. 

- Control plane model: Redwood Private supports two modes we propose to test: 
  * Local-only control plane (pull-free): a customer-hosted controller + operator UI that never initiates outbound connections; agents on the GPU nodes accept inbound, authenticated commands. All control communication is over mutual-TLS and can be terminated behind your bastion.
  * Brokered (optional) control plane: for customers who accept limited egress, we can run a control plane appliance in VPC that connects on a scheduled, auditable heartbeat and only receives metadata, never raw request payloads.

- Audit and KV persistence: logs and KV checkpoints can be configured to write to your on-prem S3-compatible object store or to an HSM-backed vault you manage. We do not persist full prompt payloads outside of your environment in the local-only mode.

Next tests we propose for the POC: 
1) Network connectivity verification: inbound-only handshake to agent on a temporary bastion IP; certificate exchange and mTLS verification. (Ben will own.)
2) Control plane blackbox: demonstrate a 24-hour window with no outbound egress while performing inference from your cluster.
3) Audit trace review: produce an audit log sample showing per-request metadata and requester identity without storing prompt text.

Ben — can you please post the test plan + exact commands (scp/ssh curl examples, cert subjects we need to import) in the Drive link and confirm the time for Tue 23 10:00 EDT?

Alan — once Ben posts the test artifacts we can hand this to your security team; Marissa will follow with PO/contract options for a 30–60 day isolated POC.

— Soojin

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Gates <alan.gates@greenfieldfin.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Jun 2028 10:35:00 +0000
Subject: Tech session deliverables & network test commands

Alan / team — thanks for scheduling the session. Below are the immediate artifacts and sample commands we'll run during the Tuesday demo. I'm dropping the most relevant excerpts here and posted the full text to the Drive link in Soojin's original email.

1) mTLS handshake check (inbound-only) - On your bastion host run:
  - sudo openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -out gf-bastion.key.pem
  - sudo openssl req -new -key gf-bastion.key.pem -subj "/CN=gf-bastion.greenfieldfin.com" -out gf-bastion.csr
  - We'll provide a CA cert to sign the CSR for mutual auth.
  - Test curl: curl --http1.1 --cert client.pem --key client.key --cacert ca.pem https://<agent-ip>:8443/healthz

2) Control-plane behavior test: 24-hour offline window - Procedure: we will perform inference against the local agent while disabling any outbound connections from that host, and capture network traces (tcpdump) + process list. Expected outcome: inference continues with zero outbound flow to third-party hosts.

3) Audit log sample (redacted) - We'll generate a sanitized log file containing request_id, model_id, timestamp, and user_id (no prompt text) and stream it to your S3-compatible store for validation.

Attachments uploaded to Drive: 
- network-test-plan.md (full commands and pre-checklist)
- controlplane-feasibility-matrix.xlsx (detailed row-level mapping vs HypCloud)

If you can share a jump host IP and a point of contact for firewall rules, I will sync credentials and our CA cert before the session. Looking forward to the demo.

— Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
